title: `organizationContext` — the operating-scope accessor re-rooting the tenantOwned write stamp, behind every backend's fail-closed `x-org-context` switch gate
note: The accessor lands only with its gate, so this fixture is what puts BOTH in front of all five compile tiers: the stamp (`tenantId := organizationContext.org`) and an operation body read lower to the derived principal member `currentUser.operatingOrg`, and every backend's auth layer emits the gate that sets it.  No `test e2e` block and no wire golden: no wire shape is new (the accessor never reaches the wire), and the runtime proof — an admitted switch stamps, a refused switch 403s with no write, a forged header on a claim-less token 403s, reads stay principal-anchored — is the booted `tenancy-org-context*` leg of tenancy-e2e.

apiCaller.e2eLess: RUNTIME HOME IS TENANCY-E2E (M-T3.6 items 3+5, `organizationContext`).  The subject is a REQUEST HEADER (`x-org-context`) that each backend's auth middleware validates before routing, which the `test e2e` vocabulary cannot set — and, like `tenancy-hierarchy` above, a switch is a statement about principals in different parts of the tree.  The booted `tenancy-org-context*` leg drives all four arms on five backends (own-org switch → stamped; any other org → 403 with no write; forged header on a claim-less token → 403; reads stay principal-anchored). RE-CHECKED in wave C3 packet 3a: still true — `test/e2e/tenancy-org-context .test.ts` is that leg, and the `test e2e` renderer has no header form.  The no-switch default the behavioural tier COULD drive is `tenancy-hierarchy`'s cell, which waits on #2976's registry-row principal.  Reasoned entry.
